12 inches near Red Dog Mine and 12 to 18 inches in the Western
Brooks Range. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

heaviest precipitation is expected Tuesday and Wednesday. The
heaviest snow is expected Wednesday. Temperatures cool Wednesday
into Thursday.

vehicle in case of an emergency.

properties.areaDesc: Cabo Rojo, PR; Guanica, PR; Lajas, PR
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 6:50AM AST until October 28 at 8:45AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Cabo Rojo in Puerto Rico...
Guanica in Puerto Rico...
Lajas in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM AST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Dangerous flows
over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 649 AM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 28 at 5:39AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 8 PM
EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.3 feet MLLW at
the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHEN...From noon to 3 PM PDT Wednesday. High tide is at 1:13 PM
at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:

will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.
